title: After Trump: The future of Democratic foreign policy  – European Council on Foreign Relations
gist: ECFR podcast in which Mark Leonard, Nevada Joan Lee and Stephen Wertheim discuss what the November 3rd US midterms mean for Trump's remaining term and for future Democratic foreign policy. The framing holds that even a Democratic Congress may not change America's 'chaotic and increasingly predatory' foreign policy, making the 2028 Democratic agenda the key question for Europe.

insights.claim: The US midterms on November 3rd see Democrats hoping to win back the House of Representatives and perhaps the Senate.
insights.speaker: Nevada Joan Lee, Mark Leonard, Stephen Wertheim
insights.so_what: Control of Congress shapes fiscal, trade and sanctions policy for the rest of Trump's term.
insights.locator: The US midterm elections take place

insights.claim: America's allies must wait to see whether a Democratic Congress could change what the episode calls America's chaotic and increasingly predatory foreign policy.
insights.speaker: Nevada Joan Lee, Mark Leonard, Stephen Wertheim
insights.so_what: Investors should not assume a Democratic Congress meaningfully constrains US foreign-policy volatility.
insights.quote: America’s global allies, however, will have to wait and see whether a Democratic Congress would be able to change America’s chaotic and increasingly predatory foreign policy.
insights.locator: The US midterm elections take place

insights.claim: The central question for Europe is what kind of foreign policy Democrats would implement if they win back the presidency in 2028.
insights.speaker: Nevada Joan Lee, Mark Leonard, Stephen Wertheim
insights.so_what: Long-horizon US policy uncertainty persists beyond the midterms.

source_meta.author: Nevada Joan Lee, Mark Leonard, Stephen Wertheim
